summary: A brownstone tower of 1802 on a narrow island off Guilford, once a fog-signal testing ground and a keeper's family home, now a tern refuge with a closed light.

lens.where: taken to New Haven for safekeeping after 1976

access.note: Boat only; grounds and tower closed except for an occasional open house; tern nesting refuge.

notes_for_editor: Mostly NRHP, LighthouseFriends and New England Lighthouses (both second-hand for keeper anecdotes); no newspapers read (loc.gov queue too slow). Disagreements kept in text: distance offshore (5 vs 3.5 mi), tower height (36 ft 8 in vs 40 ft), lens 1856 vs 1873 first record, dwelling 1858 vs 1871, typhons 1932 vs 1934, Griffing 1812 vs 1813, Zuius left 1941 vs 1943. Surname spellings Faulkner/Falkner vary. Roster lines not matched by position. Frank Parmele (USLHS 1883-86, NEL 1884-90) and the 1888 birth anecdote were left out because of the date conflict. Moses F. Webb and E. A. Woodward wrecks and the Jensen newspaper text are LighthouseFriends only; the Shoreline Times date is not given. Mary M. Brooks' relation to Oliver is not stated. Erosion project dates differ: GPA says Sept 2000 to 2001, LighthouseFriends 2000-2002. Dock/pier and 'Marcus Edwards' 1900 schooner (LHB 1901) not used because the light-vessel is unclear. Fact-check 2026-10-27: nomination gives 1902 engine house and 1903 powerhouse; both now stated.
